lens.summary: The imaging manifestations of adult-onset Coats disease differ from those in children. This study explored the multimodal imaging features of adult-onset Coats disease. lens.summary: Mental health care (MHC) utilization remains uneven among middle-aged and older adults in the United States, yet the role of comorbidity burden and other sociodemographic, socioeconomic, behavioral, and clinical domain predictors remains incompletely characterized. …
lens.abstract: Mental health care (MHC) utilization remains uneven among middle-aged and older adults in the United States, yet the role of comorbidity burden and other sociodemographic, socioeconomic, behavioral, and clinical domain predictors remains incompletely characterized. We analyzed pooled data from six waves (2019-2024) of the National Health Interview Survey (NHIS), comprising 128,261 adults aged ≥40 years. Comorbidity burden was the primary predictor, categorized as none, one, or ≥2 chronic conditions, while together with additional predictors was organized according to the predisposing, enabling, and need domains of Andersen's Behavioral Model of Health Services Use. lens.title: COlour vision assessment for the Detection of Early diabetic Retinopathy (CODER): A study protocol.
lens.summary: The current study is expected to provide evidence whether quantitative colour vision assessment can act as a functional marker of early retinal changes in diabetes and diabetic retinopathy.
lens.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Diabetic retinopathy (DR) remains one of the leading causes of preventable vision loss. However, high-contrast visual acuity, which is routinely used in the clinic, is often preserved during the early stages of the disease, limiting its usefulness in detecting early functional deficits. Colour vision is a sensitive marker for detecting these early retinal changes. This study aims to investigate whether the Colour Assessment and Diagnosis (CAD) test, a quantitative measure of chromatic sensitivity, can serve as a functional biomarker for the early detection of DR and can reflect the severity of the disease. METHODS AND ANALYSIS: This prospective observational study will be conducted at the L V Prasad Eye Institute, Hyderabad, India. lens.title: Spontaneous Achromatopsia-Like Phenotype in Albino Swiss CD-1 Mice: Retinocortical Dysfunction, Neurovascular Remodeling, and Glial Activation.
lens.summary: Spontaneous Gnat2-associated retinal dysfunction is common in CD-1 mice, causing photoreceptor loss, neuroinflammation, and ganglion cell reduction. Baseline electrophysiological screening is crucial when using this strain for vision research.
lens.abstract: PURPOSE: To characterize the functional, structural, vascular, genetic, and histologic correlates of spontaneous retinal electrophysiological phenotypes in male CD-1 mice to ensure accurate phenotyping in vision research. METHODS: Baseline full-field flash ERG (ffERG) was recorded in 205 male CD-1 mice. lens.title: Multifocal electroretinography assessment of retinal responses to myopic defocus lenses.
lens.summary: The tested defocus segment lens designs did not produce statistically detectable alterations in first order mfERG parameters in structurally intact emmetropic eyes under brief exposure. …
lens.abstract: AIM: To evaluate the short-term retinal electrical responses elicited by defocus segment lenses in emmetropic eyes using multifocal electroretinography (mfERG). MATERIALS & METHODS: A prospective cross-sectional study enrolled 14 young, healthy emmetropic participants aged 18 to 22 years with no ocular or systemic diseases. Comprehensive eye examinations were conducted, and mfERG recordings were obtained using six different condition scenarios. Retinal responses were analyzed across hexagon ring groupings defined by angular extent (Ring 1: 2.5°, Ring 2: 7.5°, Ring 3: 14°, Ring 4: 22°, Ring 5: 30°). lens.title: Real-world validation of an AI-based non-mydriatic fundus camera in the diagnosis of diabetic retinopathy in Liberia.
lens.summary: In this prospective real-world study, the offline AI-based non-mydriatic fundus camera showed high sensitivity and specificity for detecting referable diabetic retinopathy among participants with at least one gradable eye in a general outpatient setting in Liberia. …
lens.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Diabetic retinopathy (DR) is a leading cause of preventable vision loss, yet access to retinal screening remains limited in low-resource settings such as Liberia. This study evaluated the real-world diagnostic performance of an offline artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled smartphone-based non-mydriatic fundus camera for detecting referable diabetic retinopathy in a routine general outpatient screening setting in Liberia. METHODS: This prospective study was conducted at the General Outpatient Department of John F. Kennedy Medical Center, Monrovia, Liberia. Adults aged 18 years and older were recruited through convenience sampling and underwent non-mydriatic fundus imaging using the Remidio Fundus on Phone (FOP-NM-10) integrated with an offline AI system. lens.title: Performance evaluation of mainstream large language models in cataract science popularization Q&A: a comparative study of readability, quality, and educational suitability.
lens.summary: In terms of generating educational materials for cataract patient, LLMs have potential, but the output quality varies depending on the model and the topic. GPT-5 performs best in terms of overall quality and educational suitability, but its readability is not always at an ideal level. …
lens.abstract: BACKGROUND: Cataract is one of the main causes of visual impairment and reversible blindness worldwide, and it mainly affects the elderly population. Clinically accurate and sufficiently readable patient education materials play a crucial role in this regard. With the rapid development of large language models (LLMs), patients are increasingly obtaining health information generated by artificial intelligence (AI); however, the reliability of online medical information is often questionable. This study systematically evaluated the readability, quality, and educational suitability of mainstream LLMs when answering questions related to cataract. METHODS: Five mainstream LLMs - Doubao, DeepSeek, Wenxin Yiyan, Tongyi Qianwen, and GPT-5 - were evaluated based on their responses to 20 frequently asked questions (FAQs) for cataract patient, which covered five subject categories. lens.title: Co-Designing Medication Safety Interventions for Community Pharmacy: Bringing Together People Living With Visual Impairments and Community Pharmacists Using a Modified Nominal Group Technique Approach.
lens.summary: Co-design involving people living with VI and community pharmacy professionals successfully identified practical and acceptable interventions with potential to improve medication safety. …
lens.abstract: INTRODUCTION: People living with visual impairment (VI), defined as a reduction in visual acuity or visual field that cannot be corrected by spectacles or contact lenses, experience health inequalities and are at increased risk of medication-related safety incidents. This study aimed to identify challenges contributing to medication errors and to co-design potential solutions with people living with VI and community pharmacy professionals. METHODS: A modified Nominal Group Technique (mNGT) was conducted with seven adults living with VI and six community pharmacy professionals. The process comprised four stages: problem identification, solution generation, decision making and prioritisation, implementation and intervention development. lens.title: Trigonelline Alleviates Neuroinflammation in AAV-SynA53T Parkinson's Disease Model Mice: Involvement of PI3K/AKT-NF-κB Signaling and Gut Microbial-Metabolic Remodeling.
lens.summary: Trigonelline (TG), a major alkaloid in fenugreek seed and coffee, has anti-inflammatory and antioxidant activities. lens.abstract: Trigonelline (TG), a major alkaloid in fenugreek seed and coffee, has anti-inflammatory and antioxidant activities. We investigated whether TG ameliorates Parkinson's disease (PD)-related synucleinopathy and whether these effects are associated with inflammatory signaling and gut microbial-metabolic alterations. Two-sample Mendelian randomization (MR) was used to examine the relationship between genetically predicted circulating TG and α-synuclein. lens.title: Transient ocular effects of common near tasks in children.
lens.summary: Near work induced acute axial elongation and choroidal thinning in children, detectable within 10 min. Responses were similar between printed and digital tasks. This study adds to growing evidence that visual behavior may influence early ocular growth signals relevant to myopia development.
lens.abstract: PURPOSE: To quantify transient changes in axial length and choroidal thickness in children after near work and determine whether responses differ between printed and digital tasks. METHODS: In this prospective, randomized, crossover study, 26 children, ages 13.2 ± 2.2 years (16 nonmyopes, 10 myopes) completed two 30-min near tasks at 20 cm, reading printed text and digital viewing, separated by a 30-min distance-viewing interval. Axial length (LenStar) and choroidal thickness (optical coherence tomography, Spectralis) were measured at baseline and after 10, 20, and 30 min of each task. Accommodative stimulus response functions (2-5 D) were measured objectively. Data were analyzed using repeated-measures ANOVA. lens.title: Evaluating the effect of spectacle correction for refractive errors and presbyopia on cognitive function in rural older adults in China: protocol for a randomised, parallel-group, superiority trial.
lens.summary: BACKGROUND: Vision impairment and mild cognitive impairment are highly prevalent in ageing rural populations of low- and middle-income countries. Observational studies suggest that vision correction may slow cognitive decline, but robust causal evidence-particularly from rural China-is lacking, despite an ongoing randomised controlled tri …
lens.abstract: BACKGROUND: Vision impairment and mild cognitive impairment are highly prevalent in ageing rural populations of low- and middle-income countries. Observational studies suggest that vision correction may slow cognitive decline, but robust causal evidence-particularly from rural China-is lacking, despite an ongoing randomised controlled trial (RCT) in India. Our RCT will evaluate whether providing near and/or distance vision correction can slow cognitive decline among older adults in rural China, generating context-specific evidence to guide national policy and global healthy ageing strategies. METHODS: This study is designed as an assessor-blind, parallel-group, individually RCT. lens.title: Complications of Refractive Lens Exchange.
lens.summary: Safe application of RLE depends on individualized patient selection, comprehensive preoperative assessment, appropriate IOL selection, and realistic patient counselling. Because RLE involves the irreversible removal of a clear crystalline lens, its risks, benefits, alternatives, and ethical boundaries should be carefully considered before …
lens.abstract: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: Refractive lens exchange (RLE) has become an established option for the correction of refractive errors and presbyopia in appropriately selected patients. However, because the procedure involves removal of a clear crystalline lens, its potential complications and the appropriate limits of its indication require careful consideration. The objective of this review was to summarize the principal complications associated with RLE, with emphasis on their incidence, risk factors, prevention, and management. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Narrative review of the current literature on complications associated with refractive lens exchange. RESULTS: RLE is generally safe and predictable in appropriately selected patients, but complications remain clinically relevant. lens.title: Manual Deep Anterior Lamellar Keratoplasty alone or combined with lens surgery in patients with Radial Keratotomy.
lens.summary: Our results suggest that M-DALK surgery alone or combined with lens surgery provides a good balance between visual rehabilitation and safety, minimizing potential surgical-related complications in post-RK patients.
lens.abstract: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: This study aims to report the clinical outcomes of the manual deep anterior lamellar keratoplasty (M-DALK) performed alone or combined with lens surgery in post-radial keratotomy (post-RK) patients. PATIENTS AND METHODS: This retrospective study included post-RK eyes that underwent M-DALK alone or combined with lens surgery. Corrected visual acuity (AVCC), manifest refraction, and intra- and postoperative complications were recorded. RESULTS: The study included 20 eyes, twelve eyes underwent M-DALK alone, and eight eyes combined with lens surgery. lens.title: Early detection of cerebral visual impairment in young children: A preliminary investigation.
lens.summary: Children with suspected CVI scored consistently lower than both controls and preterm peers. There were no systematic significant difference between the children in the preterm group and the "suspected CVI" group across age groups. …
lens.abstract: AIMS: The principal aim of this study was to determine whether a modified version of the Evaluation of Visuo-Attentional Abilities (EVA) battery could be administered to children under 4 years of age; the secondary aim was to compare the visual outcomes of full-term, preterm, and suspected Cerebral Visual Impairment (CVI) children aged 3 to 36 months. METHODS: Several tests, derived from a modified version of the EVA battery, were administered to the children investigated, depending on their age. They were divided into three age groups (G1: 3-5 months, G2: 6-23 months, G3: 24-36 months). Children in G1 took 7 subtests, those in G2 took 9 (including 7 common to G1), and those in G3 took 13 (including 7 common to G1 and 2 common to G2). lens.title: Comparison of Anxiety Levels in Glaucoma Patients Undergoing Standard Automated Perimetry and Online Circular Contrast Perimetry.
lens.summary: OCCP is associated with slightly lower anxiety while demonstrating comparable test duration. These findings support its potential as a slightly more tolerable, accessible and cost-effective alternative for monitoring and screening for glaucoma.
lens.abstract: PRCIS: Online circular contrast perimetry was associated with a modest reduction in test-related anxiety compared with automated perimetry. Test durations were identical, and agreement between modalities was acceptable. However, Anxiety was unrelated to perimetric indices. PURPOSE: Visual field assessment is often regarded as one of the least comfortable Ophthalmological tests. This perception can induce anxiety. In this study, we compared anxiety levels and test agreement between Standard Automated Perimetry (SAP), a clinical standard that is prone to anxiety, and Online Circular Contrast Perimetry (OCCP), a web-based alternative. METHODS: We conducted a prospective, comparative, within-subject study involving 100 patients, recruited from two eye centres in Ghana. lens.title: Five-Year Follow-up of the ELZA-sub400 Protocol: Individualized Corneal Cross-linking With Riboflavin and UV-A in Ultrathin Keratoconic Corneas.
lens.summary: The ELZA-sub400 protocol safely stabilized keratoconus in 84.6% of ultrathin corneas over 5 years, with no signs of endothelial damage. Individualized fluence enabled effective treatment of corneas previously ineligible for standard CXL.
lens.abstract: PURPOSE: To evaluate the 5-year safety and efficacy of the ELZA-sub400 protocol, an individualized stromal thickness-guided corneal cross-linking (CXL) technique, in eyes with progressive keratoconus and corneal stroma thickness of less than 400 µm. METHODS: In this retrospective interventional case series, 39 eyes of 33 patients with progressive keratoconus or primary ectasia and stromal thickness between 214 and 398 µm underwent CXL using the ELZA-sub400 protocol. Following epithelial removal and riboflavin loading, ultraviolet-A irradiation at 3 mW/cm2 was applied for durations tailored to stromal thickness, targeting a demarcation line (DL) 70 µm anterior to the corneal endothelium. lens.title: Visual Performance of a Novel Intraocular Lens With Higher-Order Aspheric Design Optimized for Intermediate Vision.
lens.summary: This enhanced monofocal IOL provided excellent distance visual acuity, functional intermediate vision, preserved contrast sensitivity, and limited overall dependence on pupil size.
lens.abstract: PURPOSE: To evaluate the visual performance of an enhanced monofocal intraocular lens (IOL) and the influence of pupil size. METHODS: This prospective, observational, single-center study was conducted at Hospital Clínico San Carlos (Madrid, Spain). Patients undergoing cataract surgery with an enhanced monofocal IOL (enVista Aspire; Bausch + Lomb, Inc) were included. Postoperative monocular assessments were performed under photopic conditions at 3 months. Uncorrected and corrected visual acuity were measured at distance (4 m), intermediate (66 cm), and near (40 cm). Defocus curves and photopic contrast sensitivity were assessed, and automated refraction was compared with manifest refraction. lens.summary: Implantation of the AT ELANA 841P provided reliable refractive and visual outcomes, high rates of spectacle independence, and corrected and uncorrected VA at all distances. …
lens.abstract: PURPOSE: To evaluate the effectiveness and safety of a new trifocal intraocular lens (IOL) in patients with age-related cataracts 12 months after surgery. METHODS: This prospective, noncomparative, multicenter study included 122 patients (244 eyes) undergoing cataract surgery with bilateral implantation of the AT ELANA 841P. At 12 months postoperatively, refraction and binocular visual acuity (VA) at distance (4 m), intermediate (80 cm), and near (40 cm) were measured. Visual symptoms and spectacle independence were subjectively evaluated. Safety assessment included the rate of ocular adverse events (AEs), posterior capsule opacification (PCO), IOL tilt and decentration, and glistening formation. lens.title: MiKid-QA: construction and performance evaluation of a paediatric myopia education question-answering model.
lens.summary: Specialised fine-tuning on curated myopia-related datasets was associated with higher expert-rated correctness and safety in standardised myopia education scenarios. MiKid-QA may serve as an auxiliary educational tool to support patient communication in myopia care, although further external validation and prospective clinical studies are …
lens.abstract: BACKGROUND: The surging prevalence of paediatric myopia has overwhelmed clinical education services. While general-purpose large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used for medical information, they often lack the domain-specific precision required for specialised care. This study aimed to develop and evaluate Myopia in Kids Question-Answering (MiKid-QA), a paediatric myopia education question-answering model fine-tuned to support standardised patient education. METHODS: We conducted a cross-sectional evaluation study. MiKid-QA was developed by fine-tuning the Qwen2.5-32B model using low-rank adaptation (LoRA) on curated professional datasets (2015-2025), including textbooks and expert consensus. lens.title: Precision and reliability in tonometry: Comparison of Corvis ST and iCare in glaucoma patients on the Ecuadorian coast.
lens.summary: The biomechanically corrected bIOP yielded the most consistent, corneal-thickness-independent estimates of IOP. Although iCare remains convenient for screening, bIOP measurements appear superior for precise monitoring and therapeutic decision-making in glaucoma care.
lens.abstract: BACKGROUND: This study aimed to compare IOP or tonometric measurements obtained with the Corvis ST and the iCare rebound tonometer in glaucoma patients seen at an ophthalmology center on the Pacific coast of Ecuador. METHODS: This study retrospectively reviewed clinical records obtained between June 2023 and January 20 across six institutional sites. A total of 434 patients with bilateral glaucoma met the inclusion criteria. Each participating site had a single trained examiner responsible for all measurements during the study period, ensuring consistency within each location. Mean differences between instruments were evaluated using repeated measures analysis, and inter-method agreement was assessed using Bland-Altman plots. lens.title: Impact of retinal break location on surgical outcomes in primary uncomplicated rhegmatogenous retinal detachment: Superior versus inferior breaks.
lens.summary: The presence of at least one inferior retinal break was associated with lower 6-month anatomical success and reduced redetachment-free survival. The findings regarding concurrent phacoemulsification and tamponade choice should be interpreted cautiously because of limited subgroup sizes.
lens.abstract: PURPOSE: To compare the anatomical and functional outcomes of pars plana vitrectomy (PPV) for primary uncomplicated rhegmatogenous retinal detachment (RRD) with superior versus inferior retinal breaks. METHODS: This retrospective study included 675 eyes of 675 patients, of which 476 had exclusively superior breaks and 199 had at least one inferior break. Patients underwent primary PPV with air or gas endotamponade (SF₆, C2F₆ or C₃F₈) between January 2015 and March 2025. The primary outcome was single-surgery anatomical success at 6 months. Redetachment-free survival was analysed using Kaplan-Meier estimates and the log-rank test. Secondary analyses included final anatomical success, tamponade choice, concurrent phacoemulsification and postoperative best-corrected visual acuity. lens.title: Association of systemic aging and frailty with retinal alterations: insights from an integrated exposome and metabolome framework.
lens.summary: Systemic aging alters ocular structures and plasma metabolome, yet relationships between multidimensional biological aging, environmental exposomes, plasma metabolism, and retinal changes remain uncharacterized. This study evaluated how these phenotypic networks align with retinal structural variations. …
lens.abstract: Systemic aging alters ocular structures and plasma metabolome, yet relationships between multidimensional biological aging, environmental exposomes, plasma metabolism, and retinal changes remain uncharacterized. This study evaluated how these phenotypic networks align with retinal structural variations. Following rigorous screening, 45,542 UK Biobank participants (2006-2010) were analyzed. Systemic aging was quantified using PhenoAge acceleration, Klemera-Doubal method age acceleration (KDM-BA), and a frailty index (FI). lens.title: Preoperative Higher-Order Aberrations as Predictors of Visual Acuity Changes Following Presbyopia-Correcting (PCIOL) and Aspheric Monofocal Intraocular Lens Implantation.
lens.summary: Preoperative HOA measurements showed statistically significant though modest associations with changes in uncorrected visual acuities. In some instances, the estimated change improved by including information regarding preoperative refractive error. Validation in larger cohorts is required before clinical implementation.
lens.abstract: PURPOSE: To determine if preoperative ocular higher order aberrations (HOAs) were associated with changes in uncorrected distance (UCDVA), intermediate (UCIVA), near (UCNVA), corrected distance at reduced contrast (CDVA 10% and 25%) logMAR acuities after PCIOL or aspheric IOL implantation. lens.title: Neuro-ophthalmological disturbances in pediatric posterior fossa tumors: Prevalence, risk factors, and outcomes.
lens.summary: Neuro-ophthalmological disturbances are common in pediatric PF tumors and evolve throughout treatment. Regular ophthalmologic examinations, including detailed orthoptic assessments, are essential for timely intervention.
lens.abstract: BACKGROUND: Neuro-ophthalmological disturbances present frequently in pediatric posterior fossa (PF) tumors, contributing significantly to morbidity. This study evaluates their prevalence, risk factors, and outcomes in affected children. METHODS: This retrospective study analyzed 119 children with PF tumors treated over a decade at a tertiary care center, including 94 presenting at initial diagnosis and 25 at relapse. Clinical and ophthalmologic evaluations were performed preoperatively and 3 months, 1 year, and 2 years postoperatively. Prevalence of visual disturbances, central and/or peripheral oculomotor dysfunctions, optic nerve changes, and corrective ophthalmological interventions, were evaluated over time. lens.title: Visual Impairment and Blindness in Indian Myopes Aged 10-40 Years: A Multicenter Hospital-Based Study.
lens.summary: In this large hospital-based cohort, VI was present in about 1% of young and middle-aged individuals (10 to 39.9 years) with myopia and in 4% of those with high myopia. The occurrence of VI was 15 times higher in individuals with myopia-related retinal lesions than in those without retinal changes.
lens.abstract: PURPOSE: The objective of this study was to investigate the proportion of individuals with visual impairment (VI) and blindness due to myopia based on age, gender, magnitude of myopia, and myopia-related retinal changes using a large-scale database from two large tertiary-level eye care networks in India. DESIGN: Retrospective study. PARTICIPANTS: A total of 46 162 individuals with myopia (≤ -0.50) aged >10 to <40 years were included. METHODS: The electronic medical record data of myopic individuals who visited two tertiary eye care centers in India between January 2018 and December 2018 were analyzed. They underwent a comprehensive ophthalmic examination, which included measuring best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA) by subjective refraction and evaluating the fundus using dilated indirect ophthalmoscopy. lens.summary: Home based VPL was associated with significant improvements in CSF in PD; however, the absence of a control group means that these findings remain preliminary.
lens.abstract: PURPOSE: To assess whether visual perceptual learning (VPL) enhances contrast sensitivity function (CSF) in Parkinson's disease (PD); as a secondary exploratory aim, to describe whether the two protocols targeting different spatial frequency ranges produced differential effects. METHODS: Seventeen patients with PD were randomized to two VPL protocols using dichoptic Gabor patch video-games for 30 minutes/day, six days/week, over 8 weeks. The M-H group trained at 8-16 cpd and the L-M group at 0.5-2 cpd. CSF was measured at baseline, 2, 4, and 8 weeks. BCVA and VIPD-Q were assessed at baseline and 8 weeks. RESULTS: Significant progressive improvements in CSF were observed across all spatial frequencies and in the area under the log CSF curve from 1 month of training (p<0.001). lens.title: Adapting Falls Prevention Evidence for People with Charles Bonnet Syndrome Across Clinical and Community Settings.
lens.summary: Charles Bonnet Syndrome (CBS) refers to visual hallucinations associated with a decline in vision. Historically, the functional effects of CBS have focused on its psychological impacts, but recent work has highlighted that CBS may also lead to physical outcomes by causing and increasing susceptibility to falls. …
lens.abstract: Charles Bonnet Syndrome (CBS) refers to visual hallucinations associated with a decline in vision. Historically, the functional effects of CBS have focused on its psychological impacts, but recent work has highlighted that CBS may also lead to physical outcomes by causing and increasing susceptibility to falls. As awareness of CBS among sight loss and falls prevention specialists is low, its role in the sight loss and falls mechanism may be missed. A falls prevention approach for CBS-related falls spanning primary, secondary, and community services is indicated to ensure this potential contributory factor is not overlooked.

lens.title: Effectiveness of 0.02% and 0.04% Atropine Therapy for Myopia Control in Czech Children: The MARS Trial.
lens.summary: Nightly 0.02% and 0.04% atropine reduced axial elongation and myopia progression over 12 months compared with placebo. The trial was not designed or powered to establish equivalence between the active doses; within this sample, no statistically significant difference was detected between them.
lens.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Low-dose atropine eye drops slow childhood myopia progression, but randomized evidence in European children and for intermediate concentrations remains limited. This study evaluated 0.02% and 0.04% atropine for 12-month myopia control in Czech children. METHODS: The MARS study was an investigator-initiated, phase IIIb, multicenter, randomized, double-masked, placebo-controlled trial. Children aged 6-11 years with documented accelerated prerandomization axial length (AL) elongation and cycloplegic spherical equivalent refraction (SER) from -0.50 to -4.75 D were randomized 2:1:1 to nightly 0.02% atropine, 0.04% atropine, or placebo. The primary endpoint was the between-group difference in AL change at Month 12 for 0.02% atropine versus placebo. Linear mixed-effects models accounted for inter-eye correlation. lens.title: Taxon-specific oral mycobiome differences and bacterial-fungal associations in kidney transplant recipients and donors.
lens.summary: These findings suggest that oral microbiome differences between kidney transplant recipients and donors are more apparent in specific taxonomic changes, particularly the reduction in Malassezia, and in the relative organisation of central community members than in broad shifts in overall microbial composition.
lens.abstract: AIMS: This study characterised the pre-transplant salivary mycobiome of kidney transplant recipients and living donors and investigated cross-kingdom associations with the bacteriome. METHODS AND RESULTS: Mycobiome profiling was performed using ITS sequencing of donor and recipient samples, while paired bacteriome data were obtained from our previous study. No significant differences in fungal or bacterial alpha diversity or beta diversity were detected between recipients and donors, indicating an absence of broad community-level separation. Malassezia and Candida were the dominant fungal genera in both groups. Differential abundance analyses using ANCOM-BC2 and DESeq2 consistently identified lower Malassezia abundance in recipients, alongside predominantly lower abundance of several bacterial taxa. lens.summary: Orthokeratology lenses worn for approximately 12 months showed greater grayscale-derived visible surface alteration and higher P. aeruginosa adhesion than unworn lenses. These laboratory findings do not establish an increased clinical infection risk or an optimal replacement interval and require prospective clinical validation.
lens.abstract: PURPOSE: To compare grayscale-derived visible surface characteristics and Pseudomonas aeruginosa adhesion between unworn orthokeratology lenses and lenses worn for approximately 12 months, and to explore associations between grayscale-derived parameters and bacterial adhesion. METHODS: Sixty orthokeratology lenses were analyzed, including 20 unworn lenses and 40 lenses worn for approximately 12 months. Each worn lens was collected from a different wearer during routine replacement. Standardized slit-lamp images were analyzed with ImageJ to obtain mean gray value and gray-level standard deviation within the central 6.0-mm optical zone. In vitro P. aeruginosa adhesion was quantified as log10-transformed colony-forming units. lens.title: Hyperopic reserve, early myopia risk and screening strategies in children: A multi-regional analysis from the CREAM-KIDS consortium.
lens.summary: Reduced hyperopic reserve (HR) in early childhood is a strong predictor of future myopia. A harmonized dataset from the CREAM-Kids Consortium was utilized to assess regional differences in HR. …
lens.abstract: Reduced hyperopic reserve (HR) in early childhood is a strong predictor of future myopia. A harmonized dataset from the CREAM-Kids Consortium was utilized to assess regional differences in HR. Among 7-year olds, mean (SD) HR was 1.44 (1.17) D in Europe, 1.32 (0.80) D in Australia, 0.78 (0.89) D in Hong Kong, and 0.59 (0.66) D in Singapore (p < 0.001). The annualized decline in HR was -0.12 D/year among European-Australian followed from age 6.73 (0.64) to 11.64 (1.49), and -0.35 D/year among Asian followed from age 7.71 (0.77) to 10.71 (0.77). In European-Australian aged 6-7, the sensitivity and specificity of myopia screening was 67%-75% and 98%, and in Asian aged 4-9, 92%-99% and 70%-77%, respectively. lens.title: Association of Treatment Decentration with Early Outcomes Following SMILE Pro: A Secondary Analysis.
lens.summary: Within the narrow decentration range achieved with CentraLign-guided SMILE Pro, decentration magnitude was not associated with 3-month visual or refractive outcomes. Smaller higher-order aberration induction was associated with decentration below 0.10 mm than with decentration of 0.10 to <0.20 mm; this association was not observed in the  …
lens.abstract: PURPOSE: To evaluate the association of system-recorded treatment decentration with 3-month visual, refractive, and higher-order aberration (HOA) outcomes after SMILE Pro (VisuMax 800 femtosecond laser). PATIENTS AND METHODS: This secondary exploratory analysis of prospectively collected data included 186 eyes of 94 consecutive patients. Treatment decentration-the system-recorded scalar distance between the corneal vertex and the achieved lenticule center-was categorized as <0.10 mm (n = 94), 0.10-0.20 mm (n = 73), or ≥0.20 mm (n = 19). Primary outcomes were 3-month uncorrected distance visual acuity (UDVA), residual spherical equivalent (SE), and anterior corneal wavefront HOA (6-mm pupil) with its change from baseline (ΔHOA). lens.summary: Form-deprivation myopia (FDM) was initiated by retinal responses to abnormal visual input, but how retinal metabolism was coordinated with mitochondrial and redox homeostasis remains incompletely understood. …
lens.abstract: Form-deprivation myopia (FDM) was initiated by retinal responses to abnormal visual input, but how retinal metabolism was coordinated with mitochondrial and redox homeostasis remains incompletely understood. We integrated transcriptomics, proteomics, untargeted and targeted metabolomics, U-13C6-glucose tracing, extracellular flux analysis, molecular validation, and transmission electron microscopy in a guinea pig FDM model. FDM retinas showed accumulation of glycolytic intermediates and lactate, increased glucose-derived carbon contribution to lactate, and upregulation of GLUT1, HK2, PFKFB3, PKM, and LDHA. lens.title: Restorative and regenerative therapies for vision loss.
lens.summary: Reversing blindness and restoring functional vision remains a central challenge in biomedical engineering. Advances in ocular prosthetics have enabled limited recovery of light perception, motion detection, and coarse object recognition through anterior segment devices such as keratoprostheses and through posterior segment interfaces incl …
lens.abstract: Reversing blindness and restoring functional vision remains a central challenge in biomedical engineering. Advances in ocular prosthetics have enabled limited recovery of light perception, motion detection, and coarse object recognition through anterior segment devices such as keratoprostheses and through posterior segment interfaces including retinal, suprachoroidal, optic nerve, and cortical implants. Parallel progress in organ-on-a-chip systems and retinal organoids is providing increasingly sophisticated platforms for disease modelling and therapeutic development. Despite these advances, issues of long-term biocompatibility, signal fidelity, and surgical complexity continue to constrain clinical performance. lens.abstract: PURPOSE: Infantile nystagmus (IN) eye oscillations are usually predominantly horizontal. However, the contribution of the vertical component and its relationship with the horizontal component as a function of gaze angle remain unknown. This study aimed to quantify fixation performance at horizontal gaze angles, in two dimensions. METHODS: Eye-tracking data from 17 participants with IN, fixating nine horizontal gaze positions spanning ±20°, were evaluated using a bivariate probability density function method, wherein the derived 68% isocontour of eye position samples were analyzed to quantify the accuracy and precision of fixation. In addition, the horizontal and vertical axis range (component) of this isocontour was evaluated using linear mixed models to determine how these vary across gaze angles. lens.title: XEN63 Gel Stent in Glaucoma: Narrative Review and Expert Perspectives on Patient Selection, Surgical Technique, and Perioperative Management.
lens.summary: The XEN gel stent (AbbVie Inc. North Chicago, IL, USA) is a minimally invasive bleb-forming surgical device designed to lower intraocular pressure (IOP). The 63 μm gel stent has a larger lumen than the 45 μm gel stent, creating lower outflow resistance, which may translate into greater IOP-lowering potential. …
lens.abstract: The XEN gel stent (AbbVie Inc. North Chicago, IL, USA) is a minimally invasive bleb-forming surgical device designed to lower intraocular pressure (IOP). The 63 μm gel stent has a larger lumen than the 45 μm gel stent, creating lower outflow resistance, which may translate into greater IOP-lowering potential. However, the comparative evidence base remains limited, heterogeneous, and largely retrospective; the magnitude and durability of any advantage over the 45 μm device should be interpreted cautiously. This narrative review summarizes the currently available evidence and expert surgical perspectives on patient selection, pre- and intraoperative practices, implantation technique, and postoperative practices with the 63 μm gel implant. lens.title: Dry Eye Symptoms Among Adults Aged 40 Years and Older in Gaza During Humanitarian Crisis: Prevalence and Associated Factors.
lens.summary: DED symptoms were nearly universal in this convenience sample. Greater symptom burden was associated with psychological distress and displacement context, although specific environmental exposures were not measured directly.
lens.abstract: BACKGROUND: Dry eye disease (DED) affects visual function and quality of life. In Gaza, conflict, displacement, environmental exposure, and psychological distress may increase risk, but evidence is limited. This study estimated DED symptom prevalence among adults aged ≥40 years and examined associated factors. METHODS: A community-based cross-sectional convenience sample of 296 adults aged ≥40 years living in houses, shelters, or tents in Gaza was surveyed face-to-face. Arabic OSDI assessed symptoms (≥13) and severe symptoms (≥33). Psychological distress was measured using the Arabic DASS-8. lens.title: Dual Mechanisms of Impaired Visual Processing in Glaucoma: Insights From Resting-State and Task-Related EEG.
lens.summary: Both resting-state and task-related EEG measures differed between the glaucoma and control groups, indicating alterations in cortical activity and visual-pathway responses. Specifically, the localized high alpha modulation deficit suggests altered top-down visual network dynamics in glaucoma.
lens.abstract: PURPOSE: To examine both resting-state and task-related electroencephalography (EEG) changes associated with visual processing in glaucoma. METHODS: Thirty glaucoma patients (mean age, 63 ± 8.26 years; visual field mean deviation, -15.41 ± 6.34 dB) and 28 age-matched controls (62.86 ± 9.19 years) underwent resting-state EEG for 3 minutes under eyes-open and eyes-closed conditions. Alpha suppression, calculated as the difference between conditions, was assessed as a measure of cognitive state transition capacity. Visual evoked potentials (VEPs) were recorded using a 64-channel EEG system during a checkerboard reversal task under monocular and binocular viewing. lens.title: Presbyopia: Effectiveness of correction strategies.
lens.summary: Presbyopia is a global problem affecting over a billion people worldwide. The prevalence of unmanaged presbyopia is as high as 50% of those over 50 years of age in developing world populations, due to a lack of awareness and accessibility to affordable treatment, and is even as high as 34% in developed countries. …
lens.abstract: Presbyopia is a global problem affecting over a billion people worldwide. The prevalence of unmanaged presbyopia is as high as 50% of those over 50 years of age in developing world populations, due to a lack of awareness and accessibility to affordable treatment, and is even as high as 34% in developed countries. Definitions of presbyopia are inconsistent and varied, so we propose a redefinition that states "presbyopia occurs when the physiologically normal age-related reduction in the eye's focusing range reaches a point, when optimally corrected for distance vision, that the clarity of vision at near is insufficient to satisfy an individual's requirements". lens.abstract: BACKGROUND: Uncorrected presbyopia can greatly impact a person's quality of life and employment prospects. Nicaragua is the poorest country in Latin America and there are no population-based reports of prevalence of presbyopia in Nicaragua. METHODS: A cross-sectional population-based household survey was conducted. The sample was selected through random cluster sampling. Adults 35 years and older were enlisted through a door-to-door method using aged-based sampling. All enumerated household members 35 years and older were asked to attend a free visual acuity screening. Autorefraction was done and then uncorrected distance vision and near visual acuity were measured for all subjects. The current study surveyed ophthalmologists, optometrists and vision rehabilitation providers practicing in Alabama. METHODS: Three mutually exclusive provider groups were identified, i.e., all ophthalmologists, optometrists, and vision rehabilitation providers working in Alabama in 2010. Eligible providers were contacted in 2010 and 2011 and information was requested regarding provider demographics and training, practice type and service characteristics, and patient characteristics. lens.title: A new portable digital meniscometer.
lens.summary: This new slit-lamp mounted digital meniscometer produces accurate and reliable measurements and provides similar values for tear meniscus radius, in human studies, to the existing VM. The instrument is suitable for use in both research and clinical practice.
lens.abstract: PURPOSE: The aims of this study were (i) to develop a new portable slit-lamp mounted digital meniscometer (PDM) and (ii) to test its accuracy and repeatability compared to the existing Yokoi et al. videomeniscometer (VM). METHODS: We developed a novel application for an iPod or iPhone, which created an illuminated target of parallel black and white bands. This was used as a portable device with which to perform reflective meniscometry. lens.summary: This is the first comprehensive study of LVS provision by optometrists in Canada. In order for optometrists to become more involved in LVS, there is a need for more LV education, provincial health coverage of optometric LVS, and better collaboration communication between LV providers.
lens.abstract: PURPOSE: To document the degree to which Canadian optometrists are involved in the provision of low-vision (LV) care and their referral patterns. To investigate the barriers to providing optometric low-vision services (LVS). METHODS: Practicing optometrists across Canada were randomly sampled and invited to participate in a questionnaire that included questions on personal profile, primary practice profile, levels of LV care offered, patterns of referral, and barriers to provision of LV care. Questions included a combination of multiple choice and open-ended formats, and included hypothetical cases. RESULTS: A total of 459 optometrists responded (response rate, 24.8%). lens.abstract: PURPOSE OF REVIEW: This study provides an overview of the three types of corneal inlays now in use for the correction of presbyopia and reviews recently published evidence of the inlays' safety and efficacy. RECENT FINDINGS: Results for corneal reshaping and refractive inlays are promising, but very limited. Small-aperture inlays are already in widespread use and have been shown to improve uncorrected near and intermediate vision without a significant loss in distance acuity or an unacceptable increase in visual symptoms. Complications have been minimal, but the inlays may be removed if necessary. They do not prevent visualization or imaging of the retina and may be retained during subsequent cataract surgery. METHODS: Two separate studies were conducted to determine the repeatability of ocular surface threshold measurements made on the same day (n = 20 subjects) and 3 months apart (n = 29 subjects). lens.title: Long-term outcomes of intrastromal femtosecond laser presbyopia correction: 3-year results.
lens.summary: INTRACOR treatment after 36 months improved UNVA to varying degrees. The effect can be explained by a corneal steepening. An initial myopic shift was reversible. Reductions especially in CDVA have to be taken into account and therefore careful patient selection and information is obligatory.
lens.abstract: BACKGROUND/AIMS: To analyse visual outcomes and corneal changes 3 years after intrastromal femtosecond laser presbyopia treatment. METHODS: In a prospective, unicentric clinical trial, 25 presbyopic patients received INTRACOR treatment (Technolas femtosecond laser) on their non-dominant eye. lens.title: A preliminary study on the visual outcomes after LaserACE for presbyopia.
lens.summary: The LaserACE procedure is shown to be safe and efficient for presbyopia correction without influencing distance vision or visual quality. However, its mechanism and long-term effects need further validation.
lens.abstract: BACKGROUND: To investigate the visual outcomes over 1 year after laser anterior ciliary excision (LaserACE) procedure for presbyopic subjects. METHODS: A prospective, non-randomized, non-comparative study. Eight emmetropic eyes of four patients with presbyopia were included in this study. All eyes were treated with the LaserACE procedure using the VisioLite erbium-YAG laser (Ace Vision Group, USA). Subjects were assessed preoperatively and at 1 day, 1 week, 1 month, 3 months, 6 months, and 1 year postoperatively. lens.title: Collaborative care of non-urgent macular disease: a study of inter-optometric referrals.
lens.summary: More widespread adoption of intermediate-tier optometric eye-care referral pathways in macular disease (following opportunistic primary care screening) has the potential to reduce the number of cases with non-specific diagnoses and to increase those with a diagnosis of normal aging changes or no apparent disease. …
lens.abstract: PURPOSE: Diseases involving the macula and posterior pole are leading causes of visual impairment and blindness worldwide and may require prompt ophthalmological care. However, access to eye-care and timely patient management may be limited due to inefficient and inappropriate referrals between primary eye-care providers and ophthalmology. Optometrists with a special interest in macular disease may be useful as a community aid to better stratify and recommend best-practice management plans for suitable patients. This study assesses such a notion by appraising the optometric referral patterns of patients with suspected macular disease to an intermediate-tier optometric imaging clinic. lens.summary: The corneal morphology and central corneal thickness returned to the original after three months of discontinuation of orthokeratology. METHODS: Retrospective study. A total of 141 patients (257 eyes) with a history of wearing and discontinuing wearing orthokeratology lenses in our center were collected. Intraocular lens optics and aberrations.

lens.abstract: PURPOSE OF REVIEW: This review outlines concepts in intraocular lens (IOL) optics and aberrations important both for current IOLs and for new IOLs in development. RECENT FINDINGS: Optical aberrations make a significant impact on the laboratory and clinical performance of IOLs, especially under mesopic and low-contrast conditions. Minimizing or correcting these aberrations can potentially improve visual function. Strategic management of aberrations can have clinical utility for extended depth of focus and presbyopia correction. SUMMARY: All IOLs affect ocular aberrations in some manner. lens.abstract: We investigated the effect of environmental hypoxia on vision in snapper (Pagrus auratus). Juvenile snapper inhabit estuarine environments where oxygen conditions fluctuate on a seasonal basis. Optomotor experiments demonstrated that visual acuity is impaired by environmental hypoxia, but not until levels approach the critical oxygen tension (P crit) of this species (around 25% air-saturated seawater). In 40% air-saturated seawater, vision was partially impaired with positive responses at M SAs of 2° and above. lens.abstract: Orthokeratology (OK) is a clinical technique that uses specially designed rigid contact lenses to reshape the cornea to temporarily reduce or eliminate refractive error. This article reviews the history of traditional daily-wear OK (1960s to 1980s) and discusses the reasons for the recent resurgence in interest in the new modality of overnight OK, using reverse-geometry lens designs (1990s to the present). The clinical efficacy of the current procedure is examined and outcomes from clinical studies in terms of refractive error change and unaided visual acuity are summarised. Onset of the effects of overnight OK lens wear is rapid, with most change after the first night of lens wear and stability of refractive change after seven to 10 days. lens.abstract: Visual factors in specific learning difficulties (SpLD) are reviewed. People with SpLD fail to achieve at a level that is commensurate with their intelligence. The commonest SpLD is dyslexia, which usually results from phonological processing/decoding deficits. Additionally, there are several optometric correlates of SpLD which may, in some cases, contribute to the learning difficulty. These correlates include binocular instability and a low amplitude of accommodation. Some people with reading difficulties and perceptual distortions/eyestrain can be helped by individually prescribed coloured filters. A visual processing anomaly is also often present in the form of a deficit of the transient visual system. The role of the optometrist is discussed.

lens.title: Noticeable, troublesome and objectionable limits of blur.
lens.summary: We investigated limits at which induced blur becomes noticeable, troublesome and objectionable. We used 15 cyclopleged subjects, a Badal optometer with lines of three high contrast letters as targets, 3-6 mm artificial pupils, and 0.0-0.7 logMAR letter sizes. …
lens.abstract: We investigated limits at which induced blur becomes noticeable, troublesome and objectionable. We used 15 cyclopleged subjects, a Badal optometer with lines of three high contrast letters as targets, 3-6 mm artificial pupils, and 0.0-0.7 logMAR letter sizes. For 0.0 logMAR size, mean "noticeable" blur limits were +/-0.33D, +/-0.30D and +/-0.28D at 3 mm, 4 mm and 6 mm, respectively, but increased by about 70% for 0.7 logMAR letters. All limits reduced by about 17% as pupil size increased from 3 mm to 6 mm. Letter size had a significant influence on all blur limits (1.6-2.1 times), but blur direction had no significant effect. Magnitudes of "troublesome" and 'objectionable" limits were 1.6-1.8 times and 2.1-2.5 times relative to "noticeable" limits, respectively. Our results suggest criteria for troublesome and objectionable blur are relatively unaffected by letter size.

lens.title: Testing visual function in the clinical setting.
lens.summary: The explosive growth of automatic examination of the eye, in particular for determining refractive corrections, invites an analysis of the strengths and limitations of these devices and their role in clinical decisions. …
lens.abstract: The explosive growth of automatic examination of the eye, in particular for determining refractive corrections, invites an analysis of the strengths and limitations of these devices and their role in clinical decisions. Subjective refraction procedures are based on a patient's visual responses and these embrace many levels of additional optical and neural processing and factors involving the higher-order nervous system and perception. Because the ultimate mission is the maintenance and improvement of a patient's visual experiences, the optometric examination necessarily extends beyond the employment of automatic devices and therefore, should include engaging the patients in tests of their visual functions.

lens.summary: The findings clearly support the validity of optometric vision therapy. Furthermore, the results are consistent with the tenets of general motor learning.
lens.abstract: BACKGROUND: For nearly 75 years, optometric vision therapy has been an important mode of therapy for both children and adults who manifested a range of nonstrabismic accommodative and vergence disorders. METHODS: In this article, the scientific basis for, and efficacy of, optometric vision therapy in such patients will be discussed. Using bio-engineering models of the oculomotor system as the conceptual framework, emphasis will be focused on studies that used objective recording techniques to directly assess therapeutically related changes in oculomotor responsivity. RESULTS AND CONCLUSIONS: The findings clearly support the validity of optometric vision therapy. Furthermore, the results are consistent with the tenets of general motor learning.

lens.summary: Retinitis pigmentosa (RP) is a leading cause of blindness and visual disability in younger people. Optometrists have a major role in detecting RP and in reducing the visual disability associated with RP. …
lens.abstract: Retinitis pigmentosa (RP) is a leading cause of blindness and visual disability in younger people. refractive.abstract: RATIONALE: Gelatinous drop-like corneal dystrophy (GDLD) is a rare autosomal recessive disorder characterized by subepithelial amyloid deposition, progressive corneal opacification, and recurrent erosions. GDLD may present during the first decade of life and interfere with visual development. It may recur after keratoplasty, complicating surgical management. PATIENT CONCERNS: A 21-year-old woman of Yemeni ancestry, living in a remote area with limited access to corneal transplantation, presented with progressive left eye visual decline and foreign body sensation since early childhood. She had long-standing bilateral visual impairment and a positive family history. Her first surgery was right eye penetrating keratoplasty (PK), performed elsewhere approximately 1 year earlier for an undiagnosed opacity. refractive.title: Corneal clarity and biomechanical stability after mitomycin C-assisted photorefractive keratectomy in low, moderate, and high myopia.
refractive.summary: MMC-assisted PRK demonstrated favorable 12-month refractive, visual, densitometric, and biomechanical outcomes across low, moderate, and high myopia groups, with comparable postoperative stability and no observed ectasia observed during the follow-up period.
refractive.abstract: PURPOSE: To evaluate refractive, tomographic, densitometric, and biomechanical outcomes of photorefractive keratectomy (PRK) across different degrees of myopia. METHODS: This retrospective observational study was included eyes undergoing mitomycin C (MMC)-assisted PRK for myopia (with or without astigmatism) were categorized as low (spherical equivalent [SE] > -3.0 D), moderate (- 6.0 D < SE ≤ - 3.0 D), and high myopia (SE ≤ -6.0 D). Refractive, tomographic, densitometric, and biomechanical parameters were analyzed preoperatively and at 1, 6, and 12 months postoperatively. RESULTS: 145 eyes were included: 50 low, 50 moderate, and 45 high myopia eyes. At 12 months, ≥ 93% of eyes in all groups achieved uncorrected distance visual acuity of 20/20 or better, with comparable efficacy and safety indices with no loss of corrected distance visual acuity. refractive.title: Keratorefractive Lenticule Extraction (KLEx) Surgeries and Dry Eye: A Narrative Review of Predominantly Small Incision Lenticule Extraction-Based Evidence.
refractive.summary: Keratorefractive lenticule extraction (KLEx) is the newest widely adopted flapless refractive procedure. Small incision lenticule extraction (SMILE) accounts for most of the available evidence on postoperative dry eye, whereas evidence for newer KLEx platforms remains limited. …
refractive.abstract: Keratorefractive lenticule extraction (KLEx) is the newest widely adopted flapless refractive procedure. Small incision lenticule extraction (SMILE) accounts for most of the available evidence on postoperative dry eye, whereas evidence for newer KLEx platforms remains limited. This narrative review summarizes changes in dry eye symptoms, tear film parameters, corneal sensitivity, and corneal innervation after KLEx, as well as factors associated with postoperative dry eye and available treatment strategies. Most studies reported an early postoperative worsening of dry eye symptoms and tear film stability, followed by gradual recovery, usually within 3-6 months. Changes in tear production were less consistent. Compared with laser-assisted in situ keratomileusis, SMILE showed better preservation and earlier recovery of corneal sensitivity and innervation. refractive.title: Effectiveness of an Oral Health Curriculum in Reducing Dental Caries Increment and Improving Oral Hygiene Behavior among Schoolchildren of Ernakulam District in Kerala, India: A Cluster-randomized Trial.
refractive.summary: A structured school-based oral health curriculum significantly reduces dental caries and improves oral hygiene behaviors. Integrating it into schools provides a scalable, cost-effective way to promote lifelong oral health and lasting public health benefits.
refractive.abstract: BACKGROUND: Oral diseases affect over 3.5 billion people globally, with children in low- and middle-income countries disproportionately impacted. This study aimed to evaluate the effectiveness of an oral health curriculum in reducing dental caries increment and improving oral hygiene behavior among high school students in the Ernakulam district of Kerala, India. METHODS: A cluster-randomized, parallel-group trial was conducted in six English-medium high schools in Ernakulam, Kerala, India, involving 1707 students aged 13-15 years. Schools were assigned to receive an oral health curriculum delivered either by a dental professional or a trained schoolteacher. The "Everlasting Smiles" curriculum was implemented over 24 months through six sessions with periodic reinforcement, covering key oral health topics. Outcomes assessed at baseline, 12, and 24 months included the primary outcome (decay

refractive.title: Research on a New Model for Predicting Vault After Implantable Collamer Lens (ICL) Based on Structural Parameters of the Posterior Chamber.
refractive.summary: The vault prediction model, incorporating the posterior chamber structural parameter TCA, demonstrated favorable predictive performance in an independent validation cohort. It may serve as a useful supplementary tool for ICL size selection.
refractive.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To fit a new prediction model of the implantable collamer lens (ICL) vault including the parameters of the posterior chamber structure and to validate the accuracy of the new model. METHODS: Seventy patients (92 eyes) undergoing ICL implantation were enrolled in the prediction model group. Spearman's rank correlation was used for univariate analysis to assess the relationship between postoperative vault and preoperative ocular parameters. A vault prediction model was developed using multiple linear regression. An independent validation cohort comprised 140 patients (204 eyes) who received ICL implantation. All patients completed preoperative ocular examinations. Postoperative vault was measured at 1 month. We calculated the proportion of eyes with optimal vault (250-1000 μm). refractive.title: Optimized intraocular lens power calculation in refractive lens exchange.
refractive.summary: This review aims to evaluate the factors affecting the accuracy of intraocular lens (IOL) power calculation and the strategies to optimize refractive predictability in eyes with atypical anatomy, prior refractive surgery, or phakic intraocular lenses. …
refractive.abstract: This review aims to evaluate the factors affecting the accuracy of intraocular lens (IOL) power calculation and the strategies to optimize refractive predictability in eyes with atypical anatomy, prior refractive surgery, or phakic intraocular lenses. A narrative review of studies was conducted using PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science up to March 2026, following PRISMA methodology. Articles were independently screened and reviewed by two authors. Studies on IOL calculation in normal and non-standard eyes, post-corneal refractive surgery, phakic IOLs, and refractive lens exchange were included. In axial myopia, new-generation formulas or third-generation formulas with Wang-Koch adjustment can compensate for the historical tendency toward hyperopic errors in these eyes. refractive.title: Complications of Refractive Lens Exchange.
refractive.summary: Safe application of RLE depends on individualized patient selection, comprehensive preoperative assessment, appropriate IOL selection, and realistic patient counselling. Because RLE involves the irreversible removal of a clear crystalline lens, its risks, benefits, alternatives, and ethical boundaries should be carefully considered before …
refractive.abstract: INTRODUCTION AND OBJECTIVES: Refractive lens exchange (RLE) has become an established option for the correction of refractive errors and presbyopia in appropriately selected patients. However, because the procedure involves removal of a clear crystalline lens, its potential complications and the appropriate limits of its indication require careful consideration. The objective of this review was to summarize the principal complications associated with RLE, with emphasis on their incidence, risk factors, prevention, and management. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Narrative review of the current literature on complications associated with refractive lens exchange. RESULTS: RLE is generally safe and predictable in appropriately selected patients, but complications remain clinically relevant. refractive.title: Sutureless Epikeratophakia After Small Incision Lenticule Extraction: A Case Report to Correct Corneal Deformity.
refractive.summary: Sutureless epikeratophakia combined with customized surface ablation provides a safe, effective alternative for reconstructing irregular, severely thinned corneas following surgical complications.
refractive.abstract: PURPOSE: To describe a novel therapeutic approach using transepithelial phototherapeutic keratectomy (t-PTK) combined with sutureless epikeratophakia to manage a severe corneal deformity and irregular hyperopic astigmatism caused by a femtosecond laser malfunction during keratorefractive lenticule extraction (KLEx). METHODS: An 18-year-old woman presented with severe corneal thinning (residual stromal bed of 176 μm) and irregular astigmatism in the left eye following complicated KLEx. Management involved customized t-PTK (80 μm depth, 7.2 mm diameter) to prepare a regular stromal bed, followed by sutureless overlay of an allogeneic donor lenticule harvested from a KLEx. Topography-guided transepithelial photorefractive keratectomy (t-PRK) was performed 5 months postoperatively to refine the residual corneal irregularity and refractive outcome. refractive.title: Corneal Wavefront-Guided Transepithelial PRK Aligned to Comatic Axis After Corneal Cross-linking for Keratoconus.
refractive.summary: Comatic axis-aligned anterior corneal wavefront-guided TransPRK in stable post-CXL keratoconus showed favorable short-term visual, aberrometric, and topographic outcomes while preserving corneal integrity, and may represent a feasible tissue-sparing strategy for optical regularization in irregular corneas.
refractive.abstract: PURPOSE: To evaluate the clinical outcomes of a comatic axis-adjusted corneal wavefront-guided transepithelial photorefractive keratectomy (TransPRK) protocol for visual rehabilitation in patients with keratoconus previously treated with corneal cross-linking (CXL). METHODS: In this prospective, non-randomized, consecutive case series, 24 eyes from 17 patients with stable stage I to III keratoconus after CXL underwent anterior wavefront-guided TransPRK centered on the comatic axis, using large optical zones and a tissue-saving ablation algorithm (⩽90 µm total, ⩽50 µm stromal). Main outcome measures included changes in corrected (CDVA) and uncorrected distance visual acuity, corneal higher order aberrations (HOAs), keratometric indices, and pachymetric parameters. refractive.title: Are Baseline Learning Approaches Associated with Cognitive Load, and Do They Moderate the Cognitive Effects of Contextual Vertical Integration? A Prespecified Secondary Analysis of the CONVINCED-OG Trial.
refractive.summary: There was no clear evidence of moderation of CVI-related differences by learning approaches. Deep-approach scores were associated with lower ICL and ECL and higher GCL; surface approach showed no clear association.
refractive.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Effective clinical teaching depends on managing cognitive load. Contextual vertical integration (CVI), which interweaves basic-science mechanisms with clinical content within a teaching session, was associated with lower self-reported Intrinsic Cognitive Load (ICL) and Extraneous Cognitive Load (ECL) scores and higher self-reported Germane Cognitive Load (GCL) scores in the CONVINCED-OG cluster-randomized crossover trial. Whether baseline deep and surface learning approaches are associated with cognitive load, or moderate CVI's benefits, is unknown. This prespecified secondary analysis addressed both questions. refractive.title: Evaluation of Intraocular Lens (IOL) Formulae Utilizing Posterior Corneal Power in Post-Laser Vision Correction (LVC) Eyes.
refractive.summary: EVO 2.0-TK demonstrated the highest overall accuracy among the formulae evaluated in both post-myopic and post-hyperopic LVC eyes, while Barrett True K-TK also performed well, with both formulae achieving ≥75% of eyes within ±0.50 D in both LVC subgroups.
refractive.abstract: PURPOSE: To evaluate the accuracy of intraocular lens (IOL) power calculation formulae incorporating posterior corneal power vs traditional keratometry in post-laser vision correction (LVC) eyes undergoing cataract surgery. PATIENTS AND METHODS: This multicenter study (7 sites) combined retrospective chart review and prospective enrollment of adult cataract surgery patients with prior myopic or hyperopic LVC (one study eye per patient). Preoperative biometry was obtained by swept-source optical coherence tomography, and refractive prediction accuracy was compared across six IOL formulae (Barrett True K-AK, Barrett True K-TK, EVO 2.0-AK, EVO 2.0-TK, Haigis-TK, and Shammas-Cooke) in terms of trueness (mean refractive prediction error [RPE]), precision (RPE dispersion), and accuracy (absolute error metrics and proportion of eyes within ±0.5 D and ±1.0 D). refractive.summary: Within the narrow decentration range achieved with CentraLign-guided SMILE Pro, decentration magnitude was not associated with 3-month visual or refractive outcomes. refractive.abstract: PURPOSE: To evaluate the association of system-recorded treatment decentration with 3-month visual, refractive, and higher-order aberration (HOA) outcomes after SMILE Pro (VisuMax 800 femtosecond laser). PATIENTS AND METHODS: This secondary exploratory analysis of prospectively collected data included 186 eyes of 94 consecutive patients. Treatment decentration-the system-recorded scalar distance between the corneal vertex and the achieved lenticule center-was categorized as <0.10 mm (n = 94), 0.10-0.20 mm (n = 73), or ≥0.20 mm (n = 19). Primary outcomes were 3-month uncorrected distance visual acuity (UDVA), residual spherical equivalent (SE), and anterior corneal wavefront HOA (6-mm pupil) with its change from baseline (ΔHOA). refractive.summary: Primary analyses showed no overall group differences between PLE and HC participants in smiling mimicry. However, within the PLE group, mimicry was significantly negatively associated with blunted affect (r = -0.36, p = 0.002). In secondary analyses, CHR participants did not differ from HCs in smiling mimicry.
refractive.abstract: AIM: Early identification and support for individuals with psychotic-like experiences (PLEs) are essential for timely intervention and improved outcomes. Emotional mimicry, which refers to the automatic imitation of another person's emotional expression, such as a smile, is a fundamental social process that supports smooth interpersonal interaction and is known to be impaired in schizophrenia. However, its role across the broader psychosis-risk continuum remains unclear. This study examined smiling mimicry (the emotional mimicry of smiling) in individuals with PLEs and explored its relationship with key negative symptoms. Secondary analyses explored whether such patterns were particularly characteristic of a clinical high-risk (CHR) subgroup. refractive.summary: UEB was associated with minor changes in selected corneal topographic parameters and ACD. Although some changes reached statistical significance, their clinical relevance was not established. METHODS: This prospective single-center, longitudinal study included 88 eyes of 45 patients undergoing UEB for dermatochalasis prior to cataract surgery. Scheimpflug imaging (Pentacam®AXL, Wetzlar), was performed preoperatively and at two weeks and three months postoperatively. refractive.title: Efficacy of Facial Reanimation Surgery in Unilateral Facial Paralysis: A Systematic Review with a Focus on the Six-Month Surgical Decision Window.
refractive.summary: Surgical reanimation for UFP beyond six months demonstrates promising clinical trends. However, this review does not establish the definitive superiority of any single surgical technique. …
refractive.abstract: BACKGROUND: Unilateral facial paralysis (UFP) results in profound functional and psychosocial impairment. The six-month threshold is a critical clinical crossroads where spontaneous recovery becomes unlikely, yet mimetic muscles remain receptive to reinnervation. This systematic review evaluates the efficacy of facial reanimation surgery in patients with persistent UFP of diverse etiologies lasting at least six months. METHODS: Following PRISMA guidelines, we searched PubMed, Cochrane Library, ScienceDirect, and Web of Science for studies published between 2015 and 2025. Six studies involving 133 patients met the inclusion criteria. Quality was appraised using the Newcastle Ottawa Scale (NOS). refractive.title: Enhanced keratometry for IOL power calculation after myopic LASIK: a multi-device comparison.
refractive.summary: The BTK formula was highly accurate in predicting IOL power for patients undergoing cataract surgery after myopic LASIK. However, variations in keratometry values can influence outcomes. …

METHODS: A cohort of 62 post-myopic LASIK eyes from 37 patients was enrolled. Six methods were employed to estimate intraocular lens (IOL) power: Lenstar Barrett true K (BTK), Lenstar Shammas, IOL Master BTK, IOL Master BTK with total keratometry (TK), ORA and a modified Placido topography method. RESULTS: Mean prediction errors and mean absolute errors were lowest to highest for the modified Placido topography method, IOL Master BTK with TK and IOL Master BTK, respectively. refractive.title: Expected clinical and patient-centered outcomes associated with different rehabilitation strategies for severe maxillary atrophy: an international cross-sectional survey.
refractive.summary: Clinicians selecting different rehabilitation strategies for severe maxillary atrophy reported distinct expectations regarding treatment timing, predictability, implant survival, aesthetics, maintenance requirements, morbidity, and patient-centered outcomes. …
refractive.abstract: BACKGROUND: Severe maxillary atrophy remains one of the most challenging conditions in implant dentistry and maxillofacial surgery. Multiple rehabilitation strategies are currently available, including regenerative procedures, alternative implant-based approaches, and hybrid concepts. Although clinical outcomes have been widely reported, limited information exists regarding clinician-reported expectations associated with different rehabilitation strategies when evaluating the same clinical scenario. The aim of this study was to investigate clinician-reported expectations associated with different rehabilitation approaches for severe maxillary atrophy. MATERIALS AND METHODS: An international cross-sectional survey was conducted using a standardized anonymized CBCT case classified as Cawood and Howell Class VI. refractive.title: Therapeutic Excimer Laser Surgery - A Review of Current Indications.
refractive.summary: Corneal refractive procedures are considered safe and effective for correcting mild-to-moderate refractive errors. Due to the precision and popularity of excimer lasers, they have also been employed to treat other medical conditions. …

Due to the precision and popularity of excimer lasers, they have also been employed to treat other medical conditions. The present study aimed to discuss the utility of excimer laser surgery for managing medical conditions aside from natural refractive errors based on the currently available literature. PubMed and Scopus were the main resources used to search the literature as of Aug 20, 2025. The following keywords were used in various combinations: refractive surgery, laser in situ keratomileusis, laser subepithelial keratomileusis, photorefractive keratectomy, phototherapeutic keratectomy, excimer laser, indications, recurrent corneal erosion syndrome, corneal dystrophy, corneal scar, corneal scarring, keratoconus, ametropia. refractive.title: Refractive outcomes of posterior chamber phakic intraocular lens implantation with a central port design.
refractive.summary: This study showcases a noteworthy level of visual and refractive efficacy in individuals who underwent implantation of ICL V4c models. The surgical procedure proved highly effective and safe for correcting myopia and astigmatism.
refractive.abstract: OBJECTIVE: The objective of the study is to evaluate the visual and refractive outcomes of implantable Collamer lens (ICL) implantation with a new central port design. METHODS: This is a retrospective observational study of patients with myopia and myopic astigmatism who underwent procedures for the ICL (STAAR Surgical) between 2013 and 2022. Measurements were taken for uncorrected distance visual acuity (UDVA), corrected distance visual acuity (CDVA), manifest and cycloplegic refraction, and intraocular pressure. refractive.title: Prevention and Treatment of Iatrogenic Keratectasia.
refractive.summary: Iatrogenic keratectasia can occur as a postoperative complication following refractive laser surgery. Biomechanical weakening and the resulting steepening of the remaining corneal tissue lead to progressive myopia and irregular astigmatism, associated with a significant loss of visual acuity. …
refractive.abstract: Iatrogenic keratectasia can occur as a postoperative complication following refractive laser surgery. Biomechanical weakening and the resulting steepening of the remaining corneal tissue lead to progressive myopia and irregular astigmatism, associated with a significant loss of visual acuity. The incidence of iatrogenic keratectasia is reported in the literature to range from 0.04% to 0.6%, with the risk being higher after KLEx and LASIK than after PRK. However, due to advances in preoperative diagnostic techniques and surgical procedures, incidence estimates from older studies may be only partially applicable to current clinical practice. Risk factors include a thinner cornea prior to surgery, higher myopia, genetic predisposition or undetected keratoconus. refractive.summary: Compared with LASIK, SMILE Pro was associated with fewer postoperative corneal HOAs and better preservation of corneal asphericity. Although higher-order optical quality was comparable between the two procedures, postoperative corneal densitometry was associated with higher-order optical quality only after SMILE Pro. …
refractive.abstract: PURPOSE: To compare postoperative changes in corneal higher-order aberrations (HOAs), densitometry, and optical quality following SMILE Pro and laser in situ keratomileusis (LASIK), and to investigate the relationship between corneal densitometry and postoperative optical quality. PATIENTS AND METHODS: This retrospective matched cohort study included 60 eyes of 30 patients who underwent SMILE Pro and 60 eyes of 30 age-, sex-, and preoperative spherical equivalent-matched patients who underwent LASIK for myopia at Hanamizuki Eye Clinic between July 2025 and March 2026. Anterior, posterior, and real corneal HOAs, spherical aberration (SA), coma, anterior corneal Q value, and central (0-4 mm) corneal densitometry were evaluated using anterior segment optical coherence tomography (CASIA2). refractive.title: Long-term outcomes of orthokeratology in eyes with myopic regression after photorefractive keratectomy (PRK): a retrospective clinical study of 12 eyes.
refractive.summary: In this small retrospective case series, overnight orthokeratology was associated with sustained refractive and visual improvement over five years in eyes with myopic regression after PRK, and no serious adverse events were observed in these 12 patients. …
refractive.abstract: BACKGROUND: To evaluate long-term (5-year) refractive and corneal tomographic changes induced by overnight orthokeratology (OK) in eyes with myopic regression after photorefractive keratectomy (PRK), with a focus on visual efficacy, mid-peripheral alignment-based lens-fitting methodology, and corneal safety. METHODS: This single-center retrospective study, based on data collected between January 2016 and March 2024, included 12 eyes (nine women and three men; mean age 38.6 ± 2.9 years) with myopic regression after PRK, representing the consecutive eligible patients who continued treatment out of 15 fitted (3 discontinued for compliance-related reasons), treated with specially designed overnight OK lenses for oblate corneal profiles.
